standard.title: Specification for Floor Door Stoppers (Third Revision)
standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements for materials, dimensions, manufacture, and finish of floor door stoppers used for holding doors open at a specific position.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the requirements for materials, dimensions, manufacture, and finish of floor door stoppers used for holding doors open at a specific position.

amendments.summary: No active amendments have been issued on this copy (NIL on this copy).

certification.description: Voluntary Product Certification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Manufacturers are encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' on bodies and packaging boxes. Compliance with IS 1823 is widely required in Central Public Works Department (CPWD) civil works specifications, military engineer services (MES) tenders, and commercial building construction contracts across India.
requirements: Body and tongue shall be manufactured of cast brass, pressure die-cast aluminium alloy, or zinc alloy, fitted with a high-durability hard rubber or plastic cushion at the extreme end to absorb physical shocks.
All floor door stoppers in a consignment of the same shape, size, and manufactured from similar materials under identical conditions are grouped together to constitute a lot.
The number of stoppers to be randomly selected from a lot for inspection depends on the size of the lot, as prescribed in columns 1 and 2 of Table 4.

All selected sample stoppers are physically checked for dimensions, materials, manufacture, and surface finish. A stopper failing to satisfy any of these requirements is considered a defective stopper.

A lot is deemed conforming to standard requirements if the number of defective stoppers found in the sample does not exceed the permissible defective count given in column 3 of Table 4; otherwise, the lot is rejected.
Observed or calculated analytical values, physical dimensions, and clearances must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960 to match the significant places of the specified limits.
